title: The Catholic Church
hook: the largest church, united with the Bishop of Rome, with the Mass at its heart

segments.voice: Yesterday, Orthodoxy: icons, incense, and iron glowing in the fire. Your line was heaven on earth. What moment of beauty made you forget where you were? Day two hundred eighty-eight.

Sunday morning moves around the planet. As the sun rises over a village in the Philippines, a bell rings and a priest lifts a round white host. An hour or so later, the same thing in Vietnam. Then in India, in Nigeria, in Poland, in Brazil at a packed six o'clock evening Mass, in a little church in Ohio with forty people and a slightly out-of-tune organ. The languages change. The music changes. In the Latin rite, the words are nearly the same, translated from one Latin book. That's the scale of the church we meet today, the largest Christian church on earth. Today's word is its name.
screen: `THE SUN MOVES AROUND THE WORLD.` → `THE SAME MASS, MANY LANGUAGES.` → `THE LARGEST CHURCH.`

segments.voice: The Catholic Church is the communion of churches united with the bishop of Rome, the pope. Catholics trace that role to Peter, and to Jesus's words to him in Matthew: "thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church." The name Peter means rock. Catholics understand the pope as Peter's successor, a sign and servant of the church's unity. Other Christians read that verse differently, some saying the rock is Peter's faith, or Christ himself. It's a very old conversation, and it still goes on. At the heart of Catholic life is the Mass. Catholics believe that in the Mass, the bread and wine truly become the body and blood of Christ, and they call the Eucharist the source and summit of the Christian life. The word Mass itself comes from the last Latin line of the old service: ite, missa est, go, it is the dismissal. Missa comes from the verb to send: the service ends by sending people out. Around the Mass sit seven sacraments, from baptism to the anointing of the sick, marking a life from birth to death. And the Catholic Church isn't only Roman. Alongside the large Latin church there are more than twenty Eastern Catholic churches, Ukrainian, Maronite, Melkite, Chaldean and others, with their own liturgies, their own customs, some with married priests, all in communion with the pope. And the word catholic itself means universal, from a Greek phrase, according to the whole. We'll come back to that word later on the path.
screen: `UNITED WITH THE BISHOP OF ROME.` · `THE MASS: SOURCE AND SUMMIT.` · `ITE, MISSA EST: GO, IT IS THE DISMISSAL.` · `NOT ONLY ROMAN: EASTERN CATHOLICS.` · then, large: `UPON THIS ROCK I WILL BUILD MY CHURCH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: learn one thing a Catholic friend loves. Settle, and breathe. Think of a Catholic you know, or knew: a grandmother, a coworker, a friend from school. What did they love? Maybe the rosary in their pocket. A saint they talked to. Midnight Mass at Christmas. The smell of the church. Hold that one thing in mind with respect. If you pray, you can pray for them, and for the Catholic Church. If you don't know any Catholics, picture that little church in Ohio, forty people and an out-of-tune organ. The bell holds the time.
The Catholic Church. The largest Christian church, united with the bishop of Rome, with the Mass at its heart.
Your line: universal. Today, ask a Catholic friend what they love about their church, and just listen. Day two hundred eighty-eight.

howItsDone: Catholics are asked to attend Mass every Sunday and on holy days of obligation, and many also pray the rosary, go to confession, and honor Mary and the saints.

fork.setup: the old Latin Mass is over. the priest turns to the people with one last line. what does it say?
fork.reveal: ite, missa est: go, it is the dismissal. the service ends by sending people out, and it gave the Mass its name.

original.note: Latin: the dismissal, from mittere, to send; the Mass's last line is, ite, missa est. The root of the word Mass.

trapdoor: what you thought: Catholic means Roman, and the Mass is just a church service.
what it means: a communion of churches, Latin and Eastern, united with the pope, with the Mass at the heart.
what a scholar hears: missa, from the dismissal ite, missa est. the Mass is named for the moment it sends people out.

notes: Editor review (282-299 pass): fixed 'the sun is moving around the planet'; cut the unmeasured 'every hour of every day, someone is celebrating Mass' and the membership number (the index's 'largest church' kept); the one Latin book is now limited to the Latin rite; 'ite, missa est' glossed as 'go, it is the dismissal' (the standard reading; 'it is sent' is a popular gloss); cut 'here's something many people don't know' and 'one of the oldest conversations'; howItsDone no longer says all Catholics attend every Sunday.
Membership: about 1.4 billion (Vatican statistics); script says 'well over a billion'.
'Somewhere on earth, every hour, someone is celebrating Mass' is a common saying; not a measured fact. Confirm tone.
Eastern Catholic churches: 23 sui iuris Eastern churches plus the Latin church (24 in all). Script says 'more than twenty'.
Eucharist as 'source and summit' paraphrased from Lumen Gentium 11 without quotation marks.
Etymology of Mass from 'Ite, missa est' is the standard view; confirm the gloss 'go, it is sent'.
Readings of Matthew 16:18 presented without ranking. Confirm the Protestant summaries are fair.
